featured_reviews.name: Vishwesh Ranadive
featured_reviews.review_text:
### Apoorva: A Hidden Gem for Delicious Vegetarian Delights

If you’re searching for a restaurant in Dadar that delivers more than just satisfying food, look no further than **Apoorva**. This pure veg family restaurant, nestled in the heart of Dadar, is a culinary haven for those who appreciate authentic Maharashtrian, South Indian, North Indian, and Desi Chinese cuisine—all served with a generous side of flavor and quality.

#### **Food Quality and Taste: A Delightful Surprise**
The moment you take your first bite at Apoorva, you’ll understand why it’s a local favorite. The food quality here is impeccable, from the freshest ingredients to the skilled preparation. Every dish, whether it’s the spicy Pav Bhaji, the creamy Butter Paneer  Masala, the crisp and savory Dosas, or the perfectly spiced Hakka Noodles, bursts with authentic flavors. The South Indian offerings, in particular, are a standout, with sambar that tastes like it’s straight out of a traditional kitchen and dosas that are golden, crispy, and oh-so-satisfying.

Apoorva has mastered the art of balancing taste with health, ensuring that the food is not just tasty but also light on the stomach, making it ideal for regular visits. Whether you’re a local or a visitor, the varied menu has something to please every palate.

Ambiance: Choices for Every Mood.
Apoorva offers three distinct seating options, catering to different preferences:
1. **Roadside Open Seats**: Perfect for those who enjoy dining al fresco, these seats give you a lively view of the bustling streets of Dadar. It's a great choice if you love people-watching while enjoying your meal. I love sitting here during Monsoon.
2. **Non-AC Inside Restaurant**: For a more traditional dining experience, the non-AC section offers a cozy, no-frills environment where you can focus on the food and conversation.
3. **AC Seats Inside Restaurant**: If you’re looking to beat the heat, the AC section provides a comfortable and cool respite from the Mumbai sun.

However, the seating area here can feel a bit cramped, so it’s best for smaller groups.

While the ambiance is simple and straightforward, it’s the food that truly shines at Apoorva. The seating might be cumbersome, especially during peak hours, but the culinary experience more than makes up for it.

**Parking: A Word of Caution**
One thing to note: if you’re planning to drive, parking can be a challenge. Roadside parking is notoriously difficult in this busy area, so it’s wise to avoid bringing a car if possible. Opt for public transport or a quick Taxi ride to save yourself the hassle.

**Location: A Convenient Spot in Dadar**
Apoorva’s location is another big plus. Situated close to major landmarks like Shivaji Park, Dadar Beach, Sushrusha Hospital, and Ranade Road, it’s easily accessible whether you’re out for a stroll, visiting a friend, or just exploring the neighborhood. Despite being in such a prime area, Apoorva maintains its reputation as one of the best budget-friendly restaurants around.

**Final Thoughts**
Apoorva is more than just a restaurant; it’s a place where food lovers come together to enjoy hearty, flavorful meals without breaking the bank. The quality, taste, and variety of the food make it a must-visit for anyone in Dadar, especially if you’re looking for a budget-friendly option that doesn’t compromise on flavor. Whether you’re in the mood for a quick snack or a full meal, Apoorva is ready to serve you with warmth and authenticity.

Next time you’re in Dadar, don’t miss the chance to dine at Apoorva—you’ll leave with a full stomach and a happy heart.

featured_reviews.review_text:

Most dishes were flavorful and well-prepared. The Puran Poli stood out – soft, perfectly sweet, and very satisfying. The Kothimbir Vadi was crispy and nicely spiced. The Seasonal Thali gave a good variety and felt wholesome.
👉 Quantity & Quality:

👉 Service & Waiting Time:

featured_reviews.name: Sumit K
featured_reviews.review_text:
Aswad Restaurant is an excellent place for anyone looking to enjoy authentic Maharashtrian vegetarian food in a clean, comfortable, and welcoming environment in dadar mumbai. The restaurant maintains very high standards of hygiene, which adds greatly to the overall dining experience.

The food is not only delicious but also very affordable, making it a great option for regular meals as well as for first-time visitors wanting to explore traditional Maharashtrian cuisine. Their **Maharashtrian thali** is highly recommended, offering a wholesome and satisfying combination of flavors. Special dishes like **Bhakri–Pithla** and **Thalipeeth** are prepared perfectly and taste truly homely.

One of the highlights of Aswad is their **Modak**, which is simply the best—fresh, flavorful, and a must-try for dessert lovers. The food is mild, not overly spicy or oily, making it suitable for all age groups and ideal for those who prefer healthy, home-style meals.

The service is polite, prompt, and courteous, adding to the pleasant atmosphere of the restaurant. Its convenient location near **Dadar Metro Station** makes it easily accessible in mumbai.

Overall, Aswad Restaurant is a wonderful choice for hygienic, affordable, and authentic Maharashtrian vegetarian food with a comforting, home-cooked feel. Highly recommended.

featured_reviews.review_text:

featured_reviews.name: Namrata Gaikwad.

Dadar Darbar in Dadar East has become one of our go to places, and for good reason. We’ve visited many times, and the experience has consistently been wonderful. Hello viewer, thank you for passing by to read the review.
We decided to try out some authentic Maharashtrian cuisine and Trupt Potoba Veg Restaurant at Dadar definitely scored on all fronts.
We intended to have their Maharashtrian thali but when tried their various starters, snacks and cool drinks, we were fully stuffed.
We would definitely recommend that you visit with your family (we are surely going to visit again) for the authentic Maharashtrian taste, very good food quality, and hospitality of the staff.
Cost wise the rates seem expensive but for the quality and quantity it is good.
Quick ratings:
Food quality (freshness and ingredients): 5/5
Food taste and authenticity: 5/5
Ambience: 4.5/5
Staff behaviour: 5/5
Service: 4.5/5
Value for money: 4.5/5

For the foodie in you who wishes to know more.... let's dive into individual item reviews that we had.
1. Sabudana vada: 5/5, taste was good. Outer surface slightly crisp and inner was properly cooked. Was served with sweet curd and coconut chutney. Worth a second serving.
2. Bhajaniche Vade combined with Kala Vatana Usual: 5/5, freshly done, balanced taste and vade were soft like puris (not the hard ones). Also they were not oily. Definitely a recommendation.
3. Misal Pav: 4/5, the dish came with kala vatana usal, farsan, onion & lemon, 2 pav, extra kat, buttermilk small portion. The misal was medium spicy and palatable for the normal eaters. What we felt a bit down was the kat, which should be very spicy, but it was normal and same as the vatana usal. So there is scope for improvement on this small part.
4. Mix Marathi snacks (snacks platter): 5/5, very good. Contained two pieces each of batata vada, alu vadi, kothimbir vadi and samosa. Definitely recommend giving a second round.
5. Solkadhi: 5/5, good taste including that of ginger and hing.

I recently visited Trupt Potoba in Mumbai after hearing a lot about its authentic Maharashtrian food—and I must say, it exceeded my expectations. I specially traveled from Pune just to try their food, and it was absolutely worth it. The taste is top-notch—rich, traditional, and comforting, just like homemade meals.

The quality and quantity of food are impressive, and the service is quick and efficient. The hotel staff is very polite and courteous, which adds to the warm dining experience. The restaurant is neat and clean, maintaining good hygiene throughout. A special touch I loved was the soft Marathi music playing in the background—it created a peaceful and cultural ambiance that enhanced the authenticity of the place.

Weekends, usually a wait time of around 10–15 minutes, which is understandable given the popularity. The only improvement I’d suggest is regarding the space—it feels a bit small and could benefit from a bigger seating area.

Overall, Trupt Potoba is one of the best places in Mumbai for Maharashtrian cuisine. Whether it’s Misal, Pithla-Bhakri, or Ukadiche Modak , Varous Thalis & so on —you’ll get the real taste of Maharashtra !

Jay Maharashtra 🚩

featured_reviews.name: Arzan Dumasia
featured_reviews.review_text:
Terttulia is one of those places that instantly makes you slow down a bit. The moment you walk in, it feels calm, warm, and inviting — the kind of space where you want to sit back, talk, and actually enjoy your meal instead of rushing through it. There’s a quiet charm to the place that sets the mood just right.

The atmosphere is tastefully done. Cozy lighting, comfortable seating, and a relaxed energy that works equally well for a casual meal or a slightly indulgent dinner. It’s not loud or flashy, just pleasant and thoughtfully put together.

Service was smooth and attentive throughout. The staff was polite, well-informed about the menu, and checked in at the right moments without hovering. It made the whole experience feel easy and comfortable.

Coming to the food, which was honestly impressive.

We started with the Truffle Fries (4/5) — crisp, well-seasoned, and generously topped with shaved parmesan and chives. Simple, familiar, but done well enough that you keep reaching for “just one more.”

The absolute star of the meal was the Grilled Prawns (5/5). Perfectly cooked, juicy, and packed with flavour. The sun-dried tomato pistou added a lovely depth and richness without overpowering the prawns. This dish alone is reason enough to visit Terttulia.

The Grilled Chicken (4.5/5) was equally satisfying. Cooked beautifully, seasoned with Himalayan sea salt, and paired well with the fiery potatoes. The merlot jus brought everything together, adding richness without being heavy.

To wash it all down, the Classic Peach Iced Tea (4/5) was refreshing, light, and just sweet enough — a great accompaniment to the meal.

Overall, Terttulia delivers a well-rounded dining experience — excellent food, relaxed service, and an atmosphere that makes you want to linger. It’s the kind of place you leave feeling content, already planning a return visit.

featured_reviews.name: Shankar Singh Rajput
featured_reviews.review_text:
Prakash Shakahari Upahar is a familiar old-school spot in Dadar, popular for traditional Maharashtrian breakfast items. My experience was mixed and mostly average.
I tried the Thalipith, which was genuinely good in taste and felt fresh—easily the best item I had. The misal was average and surprisingly mild, lacking the expected spice punch. The tea was honestly quite bad, with poor taste and no real depth.
One thoughtful and uncommon decision is that they don’t serve pav at all. While many may not like this, I actually appreciated the intent—it feels health-conscious and shows they’re thinking beyond pure business.
Prices are normal and reasonable. Seating, however, is very limited, and during breakfast hours you should expect a 30–40 minute waiting time, which can test your patience.
⚠️ Important Note:
They do not accept UPI online payments, or cards. Cash payment only, so come prepared.
Overall:
A simple, traditional place with one or two good items, long waiting times, and very old-school operations. Worth visiting for Thalipith if you’re nearby, but don’t go in expecting bold flavors or modern convenience.

I recently visited Muthuswamy Cafe, and it was an amazing experience for anyone who loves authentic South Indian food.

featured_reviews.name: Himanshi Patel
featured_reviews.review_text: Café Muthuswami in Dadar is a cozy spot that brings authentic South Indian flavors to life. Known for its crispy dosas, soft idlis, and rich, aromatic filter coffee, every bite feels comforting and nostalgic. The ambiance is simple yet inviting, perfect for casual catch-ups or a relaxed solo meal. Service is quick, and the food quality is consistently impressive. Whether you’re craving a hearty breakfast or a light evening snack, this café delivers on both taste and experience. A must-visit for anyone who loves traditional South Indian food in Mumbai with a homely touch and great value.

featured_reviews.name: Pooja Fulsundar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Mutuswami Cafe is located just outside Dadar East railway station, so it’s very easy to find and perfect for a quick stop after travel. They have both indoor and outdoor seating, which is nice if you want to sit comfortably or just grab something quickly.
We tried the strawberry milkshake & mango milkshake both were thick, chilled, and refreshing. The paper masala dosa was big, crispy, and came with good chutney and sambar. Kanchipuram idli was soft and flavourful, a little different from regular idli and worth trying.
Cheese tava rice was spicy, cheesy, and filling good if you’re very hungry. We ended with pineapple sheera, which was warm, slightly sweet, and had a nice fruity taste.
Overall, it’s a good place for South Indian food and quick snacks near the station.

featured_reviews.name: VISHAL UPADHYAY
featured_reviews.review_text: We ordered cheese pav bhaji, and masala dosa and both were extremely delicious. We loved both the items. Cost wise it appeared a little costly given the ambience, and quality of service. It was situated near Dadar railway station and is fine for some snacking.

featured_reviews.name: Gayatri
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re in Dadar and craving authentic South Indian flavors any time of the day, Muttuswami Cafe is the place to be!
This is the only café in the area open 24/7, making it a perfect spot for early breakfasts, late-night cravings, or casual meetups at any hour.
The food quality is outstanding, with every dish served fresh, flavorful, and satisfying:
Cheese Pav Bhaji – perfectly buttery with a generous layer of melted cheese that elevates the classic taste.
Podi Idli – soft, bite-sized idlis coated beautifully in spicy podi masala and ghee.
Muttuswami Special Benne Dosa – rich, crispy, and soaked in butter with a delicious traditional touch.
Spring Dosa – a unique fusion twist, crispy outside with a flavorful stuffed filling inside.
Fruit Custard Dessert – creamy, refreshing, and loaded with fresh fruits for the perfect sweet ending.
Their fresh juices are equally impressive — especially the pomegranate juice and the orange-mosambi mix, both refreshing and naturally sweet.
What truly makes the experience special is the warm and polite staff. The service is quick, attentive, and always delivered with a smile. The beautiful interiors create a clean, cozy, and welcoming atmosphere, making you want to sit back and enjoy your meal.

We ordered the mini batata wada, alu wadi, kothimbir wadi, matar pattis, mini sabudana wada, masala bhaat, and aamras puri. Every dish was flavorful, freshly prepared, and true to traditional Maharashtrian tastes. The masala bhaat and aamras puri were particularly memorable.

For beverages, we tried the kokam sarbat and sol kadhi. While the kokam sarbat was a bit too sweet for my liking, the sol kadhi was excellent and complemented the meal perfectly. For dessert, we had the ukdiche modak, which was decent but not as impressive as the rest of the food.

The service deserves special mention—it’s remarkably fast, efficient, and courteous. The only drawback is parking, which can be challenging to find, especially on weekends. Overall, Chaurang is a fantastic place for authentic Maharashtrian food and is highly recommended.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Chaurang near Shivaji Park, Dadar multiple times, and honestly, the experience kept getting worse.

The first time, the menu was actually the best part of the restaurant, they had unique dishes and good variety, though the prices already felt quite high for the quantity served. The second time, the lady staff was extremely rude, just like during my first visit. Still, I visited again because my mother wanted to try their food.

But this time, it was a complete disappointment. They have removed so many good dishes from the menu like vatanyachi usal, amboli, kajuchi usal, and many other items which actually made the place special. Now the menu feels very basic, so what’s even the point anymore?

The pricing is absolutely not justified for the quantity and quality being served. Even something as simple as extra ghee costs around ₹30, and the quantity given is extremely less.

Very disappointing overall, rude staff, reduced menu, small portions, and overpriced food.

featured_reviews.name: Nehal paghadal
featured_reviews.review_text: The Global Adda is a vegetarian fine-dine restaurant located in the heart of Dadar, Shivaji Park, perfect for both family dinners and special occasions. The warm ambience and elegant setup make it even more special, especially with their candlelight dinner experience every Tuesday and Thursday, which adds a romantic touch. We tried a mix of their signature dishes, and each one stood out in its own way. The kali miri paneer tikka was perfectly spiced and smoky, while the veg tit bits and sizzling cheese burger were absolute crowd-pleasers. The Neapolitan-style pizza had a soft base with well-balanced toppings, and ending the meal with sizzling gajar halwa and strawberry cream was the perfect sweet finish. Overall, The Global Adda offers a delightful vegetarian dining experience with great food, ambience, and vibes.

featured_reviews.name: Rutuja Gaikwad
featured_reviews.review_text: We visited Global Adda Restaurant in Dadar with a group and ordered a mix of dishes like Manchow soup, hot and sour soup, sushi, a few starters, pizza, and sizzlers. Overall, the food was really good and nicely presented, with decent portion sizes. The soups and starters stood out the most, and everything tasted fresh. Service was smooth and staff was attentive without being overbearing. The ambience has a nice, lively vibe, making it a good place for group outings. Prices felt reasonable for the quality and experience, so it was definitely worth the money.

featured_reviews.name: Sejal Jain
featured_reviews.review_text:
Had a wonderful candlelight dinner experience at The Global Adda in Dadar. The ambience was warm, cozy, and perfect for a romantic evening. The setup on Tuesday & Thursday is beautifully done with soft lights and a peaceful vibe.

We tried the Global Rock, Mexican Fondue, Deep Dish Peri Peri Pizza, Veg Miloni with Roti & Kulcha, and the Blue Rice with Spicy Peanut Butter Sauce — every dish was fresh and full of flavour. The Mexican fondue and deep dish pizza were my personal favourites.

Desserts like the Strawberry Freak Shake and Strawberry Creamy were the perfect sweet ending.

Great food, great service, and very good offers on the total bill too. Definitely recommended for date nights and special occasions.
